decisions.strings / mutability: U1 #string-formatting-and-immutability. P003-Q27 splits 3+2+3: join()/split() with examples (3m), mutable vs immutable data types (2m), why strings are immutable with an example (3m). The two 3-mark halves both land on the strings section, and the 2-mark mutable/immutable definition is the same section's table; the heading names formatting AND immutability, which is the only title covering both.
decisions.loops / digit sum: U2 #classic-exam-loop-programs. P004-Q18 splits 3+5: for vs while (3m), sum of digits (5m). The 5-mark program decides it, and the digit-sum program is literally section 2 of 'the three loop programs the paper asks for'. The 3-mark comparison is a table in the loop section one click away.
decisions.tuples / pass / for-else: U2 #for-else-and-while-else. P004-Q22 splits 4+2+2: print a tuple with a for loop (4m), pass (2m), for-else (2m). Marks favour the loop-over-tuple half, which the loops section teaches -- but 'for-else' appears in exactly one heading in the whole subject and nothing else answers subpart (iii) at all. Losing 2 of 8 marks because the page has no such heading is worse than arriving one heading away from the tuple program. Flagged: #for-loops-while-loops-and-range is the other defensible landing.
decisions.logical / identity / bitwise operators: U1 #logical-identity-and-membership-operators. P006-Q20 splits 2+6: logical and identity operators (2m), then a 6-mark trace of &, |, ^, ~, //. The 6-mark half is the bitwise trace, whose heading is #bitwise-operators-and-precedence. Chosen: the logical/identity heading, because the topic lists those words first and the bitwise heading is the immediately next section in the same page. Flagged for owner review -- at 2 versus 6 the marks argue for #bitwise-operators-and-precedence, and that is the one entry in this map where 'first word of the topic' beat 'largest subpart'.
decisions.functions / lambda: U3 #lambda-functions-and-recursion. P006-Q21 splits 3+5: user-defined vs built-in function (3m), what a lambda is and why (5m). The 5-mark lambda half decides it, and the heading names lambda explicitly. Flagged: #built-in-versus-user-defined-functions answers the 3-mark half and is one heading away.
decisions.modules / packages / scope: U3 #module-versus-package. P005-Q19 splits 4+4: (i) module vs package with an example each, (ii) global/local/class/nonlocal scope. Marks tie, so the tie-break is title specificity: the topic opens with 'Modules / packages' in that order, and #module-versus-package's heading answers (i) exactly while (ii) is one heading away inside the same unit. The LEGB heading would answer (ii) and leave (i) to the table of contents. Flagged: either is defensible at 4+4.
decisions.packages / pip: U3 #pip-and-installing-packages. P003-Q6 is a 1-mark MCQ ('identify the package manager'), so the answer is pip, not the package-vs-module distinction.
decisions.modules / datetime: U1 #datetime-in-python, NOT Unit 3. P003-Q18 asks for the output of datetime.date(2022, 12, 18) rebinding the module name. Unit 1 teaches datetime (import datetime, .date, .now, strftime, timedelta); Unit 3's module section teaches importing, not the datetime API. The stored unit (3) is wrong.
decisions.modules / functions / datetime: U1 #datetime-in-python. P003-Q32 splits 2+3+3: (a) module vs package (2m), (b) arbitrary arguments (3m), (c) code to print current date and time (3m). The two largest subparts are joined by the fact that only Unit 1 teaches the datetime call, and an 8-mark answer that cannot produce (c) loses 3 marks outright. Unit 3's module section answers (a) but not (c).
decisions.operators / modules: U1 #arithmetic-string-and-assignment-operators. P003-Q31 splits 4+4: (a) types of operators with examples, (b) an example of importing a module. Operators is the larger and the more heavily examined half here; the import example is one line that Unit 1 already demonstrates.
decisions.collections / slicing: U1 #lists-slicing-methods-and-copy-semantics, NOT Unit 2. P006-Q18 splits 5+3: (a) differentiate lists/tuples/dictionaries, (b) list slicing vs list indexing. Both halves are taught in Unit 1's collections sections; the stored unit (2) is wrong and the previous matcher sent this to Unit 1 anyway, which was right by accident.
decisions.strings / palindromes: U1 #string-formatting-and-immutability, NOT Unit 2. P006-Q17 splits 3+5: (a) how a string is represented, (b) a palindrome program. Unit 1 carries a worked 'Palindrome check -- the standard 5-mark program' with both the slicing and the loop form. Unit 2 mentions palindrome only inside #practice, which is a paper-section anchor and may not be used. The stored unit (2) is wrong.
decisions.loop control / list vs dict / prime prog: U2 #classic-exam-loop-programs. P005-Q17 splits 3+2+3: continue/break/pass (3m), list vs dict (2m), prime program (3m). Marks tie between the loop-control explanation and the prime program; the program is a single named section fulfilling the largest self-contained deliverable, and the other two subparts are each covered by a heading reached in one click from it.
decisions.file i/o / regex: U4 #file-opening-and-access-modes. P004-Q20 splits 6+2: file opening modes (6m) vs pattern matching (2m). Marks decide decisively -- 6 to 2.
decisions.files / lambda: U4 #file-object-methods-and-word-count. P006-Q23 splits 4+4: file read/write functions vs lambda. Equal marks; the file half has a dedicated heading naming read/write, and Unit 3's lambda section is one click away.
decisions.regular expressions / numpy: U4 #regular-expressions-and-pattern-matching. P005-Q23 splits 2+3+3: start()/end() (2m), re.match/split/findall (3m), numpy FFT (3m). 5 of 8 marks are core regex; numpy is one badged callout inside the same unit.
decisions.regular expressions / django: U5 #mvc-and-django-mvt-architecture, NOT Unit 4. P006-Q24 splits 4+4: regex working, then Django MVC/MTV. Equal marks, and the stored unit is 5. The MVC/MTV half is the unit's 19-mark Tier A cluster and has the dedicated mapping table; mapping this to Unit 4 would send a Unit 5 question to a different unit entirely.
decisions.file word count / mvc / django vs flask: U5 #mvc-and-django-mvt-architecture. P005-Q21 splits 4+2+2. The single largest subpart is the file word-count program, which lives in Unit 4 -- but 4m of 8m is not a majority, and the question is filed as Unit 5 while the two Django subparts (4m together) are what the unit is assessed on. Flagged for owner review: this is the one entry where 'largest subpart' and 'stored unit' disagree. Chosen: keep it in Unit 5 and let the cross-link to Unit 4's word-count heading carry the first subpart.
decisions.mvc / django: U5 #mvc-and-django-mvt-architecture. Both P003-Q34 and P004-Q21 split 3+5: MVC then Django. The 5-mark half is 'what is Django / steps to create a project', which the #why-django-and-project-setup heading answers exactly; but the topic's MVC half is 3m and MVC is the unit's Tier A cluster. Chose the MVC/MVT heading because it is the one section that names both halves in its title and its table.
decisions.django architecture: U5 #mvc-and-django-mvt-architecture. P006-Q14 is a 2-mark MCQ on MVC/MVT, which is exactly that heading.
decisions.data types / indentation: U1 #python-basics-indentation-keywords-and-comments, NOT #data-types. P006-Q16 splits 5+3: built-in data types (5m), indentation (3m). Chosen: the python-basics heading, because its title names indentation and the question's smaller half is the one with no other home. Flagged: either anchor is arguable.
decisions.basics / sequences / conditionals: U1 #lists-slicing-methods-and-copy-semantics. P004-Q16 splits 2+3+3: indentation (2m), list vs tuple (3m), if statement (3m). Marks favour the list/tuple comparison, which the lists heading covers and which the tuples heading continues into.
decisions.data types / type conversion: U1 #data-types-mutability-and-type-conversion. P005-Q16 splits 5+3: basic data types, then type conversion. The heading names both.
decisions.slicing / dictionaries: U1 #lists-slicing-methods-and-copy-semantics. P004-Q17 splits 4+4: list slicing, then dictionary. Equal marks; slicing is named in the heading title and the dictionary section is one click on.
